articles.title: The chocolate bar that melted next to a radar: the story of the birth of the microwave
articles.standfirst: He accidentally discovered that microwaves could heat food while working during World War II
articles.summary: He accidentally discovered that microwaves could heat food while working during World War II
articles.body:
D uring World War II, radar became a decisive technology for detecting enemy aircraft and submarines. Behind those systems was a fundamental component: the magnetron , a device capable of generating microwaves. In one of the laboratories of the American company Raytheon, Percy Spencer worked there, a self-taught engineer who would end up finding an unexpected application for that technology.

In 1945, while conducting tests near an operating magnetron, Spencer noticed that the chocolate bar he had in his pocket had melted.

From popcorn to the first oven

His next experiment was with corn kernels. He placed them near the device and watched as they began to pop into popcorn . He then tried an egg, which ended up exploding due to the pressure building up inside it. Those tests gave him a clue: the energy emitted by the magnetron could also be used for cooking.

Spencer then devised a metal box in which to concentrate the microwaves and heat food in a controlled way. Raytheon saw the potential of the idea and filed a patent application for a microwave cooking process in October 1945 . The patent was granted in 1950.

The first commercial model, christened Radarange, reached the market in 1947 . However, it was very far from today’s household appliances : it stood around 1.8 meters tall, weighed hundreds of kilos, and had a high price. Its size and cost initially limited its use to restaurants, industrial kitchens, and other professional spaces.

The technology needed decades of improvements to reach homes. The models became smaller and more affordable, eventually turning that accidental discovery into a common household appliance . Spencer, who amassed more than a hundred patents during his career, did not start out with a project to revolutionize kitchens: he simply noticed a melted chocolate bar and wanted to find out why it had happened.

articles.title: Pitbull and his private life: “I’m very reserved about what I do, so I don’t want to bring them into my world; it’s my responsibility as a father to protect them”
articles.standfirst: The singer is very protective of his private life
articles.summary: The singer is very protective of his private life
articles.body:
What we are used to is celebrities exposing their private lives, whether of their own free will or simply because of the exposure that comes with their profession itself. However, there are celebrities who resist the public exposure of their privacy and those around them. One of those people is Pitbull, who keeps his private life in the utmost confidentiality , choosing to keep his parental duties completely out of the media spotlight. In fact, as he told Billabong: “I’m very reserved about what I do, so I don’t want to bring them into my world; it is my responsibility as a father to protect them."

The importance of maintaining privacy

Having a private life should not be a luxury, but a necessity. It is not only good, but necessary for our well-being. It is important to understand that it can give us peace of mind and less anxiety by not forcing yourself to expose every detail on social media or to third parties. It is very stressful to have to seek extreme validation or compare yourself to others. It is a way of not owing anyone any explanations nor having to expose our loved ones or have them question your decisions as a father, husband, or person.

Being famous or well-known is not the only way to feel exposed; you can also feel that exposure on social media or in real life. But setting that exposure aside allows you to have greater focus and greater authenticity that help you build projects or go through processes in silence, allowing you to make mistakes, reflect, and grow without the pressure of feeling that you cannot fail.

Furthermore, not exposing those we love and our privacy allows us to protect your reputation and relationships as well as those of your loved ones and to have a personal safety network that limits the amount of vulnerable information.

But if there is one type of overexposure that is even more harmful, it is that of children, since it can even become dangerous for them. One of the duties we have is to ask for consent , encouraging dialogue and consulting at least before sharing any content involving minors, also helping to foster dialogue on this issue and reflection on whether it is the best course of action or not.

In addition, we must be cautious and avoid sensitive data about the minor, without showing clearly identifiable faces, nudity, school information and, of course, we should never post in real time. If you want to share something, it is advisable to keep the circles closed and strictly limit the audience to very close family members, and periodically review the privacy settings of the accounts and social networks we use.

articles.title: The curious English remedy from the High Middle Ages that scientists have reconstructed for its effectiveness against bacteria
articles.standfirst: A mixture that is now being put to the test
articles.summary: A mixture that is now being put to the test
articles.body:
Centuries ago, human beings did not have the medical and technological advances of today and, therefore, diagnosing and treating certain illnesses was an almost impossible task. In the search for a product that could relieve a patient, all around the world remedies were created that, in a way, helped those affected, and based on this a cure was developed.

In the High Middle Ages , an English remedy became very popular due to its supposed effectiveness against bacteria . Now, the scientific community has come together to recreate that mixture and thus be able to verify firsthand whether, in fact, it lives up to that medical premise or not and can be used in the future.

The main objective of this medieval remedy against bacteria

It is the Bald's eye ointment . An English physician was the original author of this recipe, which mixed wine, garlic, onion, and ox bile . Its aim was to combat styes and, according to today’s experts, its laboratory results were surprising: it was able to damage the membranes of dangerous bacteria, such as Staphylococcus aureus .

Over two weeks, the bacteria became more resistant to antibiotics than to the medieval remedy , so this ointment could now be used as a basis for the development of future mixtures that can be employed in the antibacterial fight and that represent an alternative to already known remedies.

One alarming figure is that, for example in 2021, antibiotic resistance could be associated with more than 4.5 million deaths worldwide . Remedies like this one from the High Middle Ages could serve as an example so that the medical community has more tools within reach and patients have more and better options when it comes to combating certain ailments.

articles.title: The four terrifying and enigmatic predictions of Nostradamus for 2027
articles.standfirst: The famous prophecies of the French apothecary are once again at the center of international controversy after the dark scenarios that would mark the year 2027 were revealed
articles.summary: The famous prophecies of the French apothecary are once again at the center of international controversy after the dark scenarios that would mark the year 2027 were revealed
articles.body:
The prophecies of Michel de Nostredame , universally known as Nostradamus , continue to generate an unshakable fascination as new calendar cycles approach. Written in the 16th century in a poetic format known as quatrains and grouped into centuries, their enigmatic lines have been reinterpreted from generation to generation. Historians and scholars of the occult recall that the French physician and astrologer published his masterwork in 1555, achieving enormous notoriety after the death of King Henry II of France, an event that many interpreted as his first great accurate clairvoyant prediction .

Over the centuries, occultism enthusiasts have tried to fit the seer’s verses to events of major global significance, from the Great Fire of London to the most critical moments of the 20th and 21st centuries. However, the academic community insists on maintaining a stance of rigorous skepticism toward these readings . Specialists point out that the original texts lack explicit dates and that their literary ambiguity allows them to be freely shaped so that they retrospectively match almost any historical catastrophe or contemporary crisis .

The specific linking of these predictions to the year 2027 stems from a modern method of analysis popularized by the mystic’s followers. Traditionally, many interpreters use quatrain number 27 from the different centuries to associate it directly with the current year, an interpretive device foreign to the author’s original intent. Despite the lack of scientific rigor, the arrival of this period has once again raised alarm among prophecy enthusiasts , who closely analyze the verses in search of warnings about humanity’s immediate future .

Cursed treasures and ancient mysteries

One of the most disturbing passages recovered by experts in ancient cryptography describes an oak tree struck by lightning and the revelation of a treasure hidden for centuries. The legend accompanying these verses includes a chilling warning for any daring soul who tries to unearth the riches: the prophecy states that the discoverer will suffer a violent death with a sharp object piercing their eye . This dramatic description has fueled all kinds of theories for decades about ancestral curses protecting forgotten fortunes in remote corners of the planet.

Modern researchers of Nostradamus's writings often directly associate this passage with the intense explorations carried out on Oak Island , an enigmatic island located off the coast of Canada. For generations, treasure hunters have invested millions in excavating the land in search of a supposed hidden loot, a quest that has gained enormous worldwide notoriety thanks to television productions such as the documentary program The Curse of Oak Island. Although excavation teams have recovered various metallic artifacts and historical remains, the great treasure still has not appeared .

Despite the lack of tangible evidence, followers of the prophecies insist that 2027 could be the key year in which this age-old mystery is finally resolved in a tragic way . For their part, local historians and folklore experts remind us that the supposed curse is part of the popular mythology built around the North American island and not a proven supernatural warning. The fascination with the enigmas of the underground shows how ancient texts continue to fuel the appetite for the unknown.

Armed conflicts and tensions in the Black Sea

The international geopolitical chessboard also does not escape the darkest interpretations of the quatrains for the coming cycle. Various prophecy analysts highlight verses that explicitly speak of fire, deployments of heavy weaponry, and an alleged military advance from Persian territory toward the ancient region of Trebizond . In current cartography, this geographic point corresponds to the modern Turkish city of Trabzon, strategically located in the vicinity of the turbulent waters of the Black Sea, an area historically sensitive to global security.

In contemporary geopolitical readings, the mention of Persia is usually interpreted as a direct allusion to the Islamic Republic of Iran and its role in Middle Eastern tensions. International security analysts, such as expert Jiang Xueqin, have repeatedly warned about the risks of a large-scale military escalation and massive civil unrest that could destabilize the global economy . Nostradamus's quatrains describe scenarios in which the waters of the seas are stained with blood, imagery that alarmists use to predict armed confrontations with continental repercussions.

Faced with these catastrophic readings, international relations experts urge caution and remind us that using sixteenth-century texts to anticipate modern military conflicts lacks empirical validity. Nevertheless, some interpreters suggest that Turkey could play a crucial role as a mediator in potential peace negotiations , mitigating the crisis before it reaches irreversible proportions. The ambiguity of the verses leaves multiple hypotheses open about the future of global diplomacy and stability in Eurasia.

The financial collapse and the fall of great wealth

The economic sphere is another of the fundamental pillars in the interpretations circulating about the year 2027. The verses analyzed by specialists in alternative finance describe symbolic images of gold and silver with artificially inflated values that end up being thrown into the fire and consumed by the flames. These passages suggest a scenario of widespread bewilderment in which the great accumulated fortunes lose their market value overnight, unleashing a profound crisis of confidence in international markets and shaking the foundations of the global capitalist system .

Economists and macroeconomics experts point out that this interpretation finds a curious parallel with current warnings about the uncontrolled growth of sovereign public debt among the world's major powers. From this analytical perspective, the precious metals mentioned in the quatrains would function as a perfect metaphor for the fictitious wealth and financial speculation that characterize modern markets. Financial analysts warn that the fragility of the current monetary system exposes the global economy to drastic and unforeseen corrections .

Despite the concern generated among small investors, economists emphasize that Nostradamus never predicted a specific financial crisis for 2027 and that any current correlation is the product of retrospective reinterpretation . Warnings about inflation and the collapse of overvalued assets are part of the usual economic cycles of contemporary capitalism. However, the appeal of finding in Renaissance poetry a warning about today’s financial fragility keeps the most pessimistic observers of the global economy on alert.

articles.title: In 1978, two children found a Ferrari buried in their home's garden: behind it was an alleged insurance fraud
articles.standfirst: The Ferrari Dino 246 GTS had disappeared in 1974 and was found in 1978 beneath the garden of a house in Los Angeles
articles.summary: The Ferrari Dino 246 GTS had disappeared in 1974 and was found in 1978 beneath the garden of a house in Los Angeles
articles.body:
There are discoveries that seem straight out of a movie, but happen by chance. In February 1978, two children playing in the garden of their home in Los Angeles (United States) started digging in the ground and found something they did not expect: a Ferrari Dino 246 GTS that had been buried for four years. What began as a game ended up uncovering a story of disappearance, an insurance payout, and an alleged fraud that was never completed as planned.

The children were digging when their shovels struck something strange beneath the grass. After removing some of the earth, they found some plastic and a green metal surface . The family alerted the authorities, and several officers went to the house to investigate the discovery. At first, the scene was so baffling that investigators even considered whether there might be something else underground.

The excavation revealed that what had been buried was a 1974 Ferrari Dino 246 GTS , a highly valuable Italian sports car. The vehicle had been protected with plastic sheeting, blankets, and other materials in an attempt to prevent moisture and dirt from damaging it during the time it remained hidden.

A disappeared Ferrari and an insurance payout

The license plate and the chassis number made it possible to quickly identify the car. It belonged to Rosendo Cruz, a plumber from California who had bought it new in 1974 for $22,500 . Just a few weeks after purchasing it, he reported that it had been stolen.

Since the car did not turn up, the insurance company ended up paying him compensation for its disappearance. However, the 1978 discovery completely changed the course of the case.

Years later, an informant provided investigators with a version according to which the Ferrari's disappearance had allegedly been part of an insurance fraud scheme . According to that account, the owner had allegedly hired several people to make the vehicle disappear so he could collect the insurance payout . The plan was to get rid of the sports car, but those who were given the job allegedly decided not to destroy it.

Instead of sinking it in the Pacific Ocean or dismantling it to sell its parts, they chose to bury it whole on a plot of land that was undeveloped at the time. The intention was supposedly to recover it once the matter had been forgotten. However, the place eventually became a residential area, and houses were built on the land. The car ended up beneath one of them, and no one ever came back for it.

The Ferrari was restored after its discovery

The passage of years underground left significant damage to the vehicle. Moisture had affected the bodywork and the interior, while the extraction also caused damage. Despite this, the Ferrari aroused enormous interest because of its history, and the insurance company decided to put it up for sale.

The car passed through the hands of several owners until it was acquired by an enthusiast who drove its restoration . The specialist in charge of the work managed to bring the engine back to life and recover much of its original appearance.

The sports car's story became forever linked to its unusual discovery. Its owner even decided to personalize the license plate with the inscription " DUG UP ", which in English means " dug up ". A direct reference to the four years the Ferrari spent hidden underground before two children, who were simply playing in their home's garden, brought it to light.

articles.title: Søren Kierkegaard, Danish philosopher: "Life is not a problem to be solved, but a reality to be experienced"
articles.standfirst: The famous reflection encourages people to stop treating existence as a series of challenges to overcome and instead appreciate the experiences that make life meaningful
articles.summary: The famous reflection encourages people to stop treating existence as a series of challenges to overcome and instead appreciate the experiences that make life meaningful
articles.body:
Life can often feel like an endless sequence of problems waiting to be fixed. People spend years making plans, pursuing ambitions and worrying about what comes next, sometimes forgetting to appreciate what is happening around them.

A widely circulated philosophical quotation offers a different perspective: "Life is not a problem to be solved, but a reality to be experienced."

The words are frequently associated with Søren Kierkegaard , the Danish philosopher whose work explored human existence, personal responsibility, faith and the difficulties of making meaningful choices.

Although the quotation captures ideas that are closely associated with his philosophy, there is an important detail behind its popularity: there is no reliable evidence that Kierkegaard actually wrote or said these exact words.

The wording appears to be a variation of a sentence published by Dutch writer and philosopher Jacobus Johannes van der Leeuw in his 1928 book The Conquest of Illusion. His original formulation was: "The mystery of life is not a problem to be solved; it is a reality to be experienced."

The distinction matters because the phrase has circulated under Kierkegaard's name for decades, appearing on quotation websites and in collections of inspirational sayings.

Nevertheless, its underlying message provides an interesting starting point for understanding the Danish philosopher's approach to existence.

Born in Copenhagen on May 5, 1813, Kierkegaard became one of the most influential thinkers of the 19th century. His writings challenged people to examine their beliefs, decisions and relationships with the world rather than simply accepting the expectations of society.

Why Kierkegaard believed individual experience mattered

Kierkegaard is frequently described as a founding figure of existentialism, a philosophical tradition concerned with individual existence, freedom and the responsibility people have for their choices.

One of his central concerns was the difference between understanding something intellectually and actually living through it. He questioned the idea that human existence could be explained entirely through abstract theories or universal systems.

For Kierkegaard , becoming an individual involved making personal decisions and accepting the uncertainty that accompanied them. People could not simply rely on other people's expectations to determine how they should live.

This perspective helps explain why the popular quotation feels consistent with his broader philosophy, even if its attribution is questionable.

His personal life also influenced his writing. Kierkegaard spent much of his life in Copenhagen and became particularly interested in questions surrounding faith, anxiety, love and the individual's relationship with God.

His relationship with Regine Olsen was especially significant. The couple became engaged in 1840, but Kierkegaard subsequently broke off the engagement. The experience continued to influence his reflections on commitment, sacrifice and personal responsibility.

Among his most important publications were Either/Or (1843), Fear and Trembling (1843) and The Concept of Anxiety (1844). These works examined different aspects of human decision-making and the emotional consequences of living with uncertainty.

The real author behind the famous quotation

The history of the quotation adds another dimension to its meaning. Van der Leeuw 's The Conquest of Illusion, published in 1928, contains the earlier version of the sentence, predating many of the later appearances that credited Kierkegaard .

Reference collections including Wikiquote have highlighted the disputed attribution, while the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy provides a detailed account of Kierkegaard's actual philosophical contributions.

Ultimately, the quotation remains popular because its message is easy to recognise. Life cannot always be organised into neat objectives, and not every difficult experience has an immediate solution.

Its appeal lies in encouraging people to appreciate relationships, unexpected opportunities and ordinary moments instead of becoming consumed by what they have yet to achieve.

Kierkegaard died in Copenhagen on November 11, 1855, aged 42, but his influence on philosophy, theology and literature continues.

Whether readers encounter the famous sentence under his name or Van der Leeuw 's, its central idea remains relevant: existence is not simply something to manage or control. It is something to participate in, understand and experience.

A widely circulated philosophical quotation offers a different perspective: "Life is not a problem to be solved, but a reality to be experienced."

The words are frequently associated with Søren Kierkegaard , the Danish philosopher whose work explored human existence, personal responsibility, faith and the difficulties of making meaningful choices.

Although the quotation captures ideas that are closely associated with his philosophy, there is an important detail behind its popularity: there is no reliable evidence that Kierkegaard actually wrote or said these exact words.

The wording appears to be a variation of a sentence published by Dutch writer and philosopher Jacobus Johannes van der Leeuw in his 1928 book The Conquest of Illusion. His original formulation was: "The mystery of life is not a problem to be solved; it is a reality to be experienced."
The distinction matters because the phrase has circulated under Kierkegaard's name for decades, appearing on quotation websites and in collections of inspirational sayings.
Nevertheless, its underlying message provides an interesting starting point for understanding the Danish philosopher's approach to existence.

Born in Copenhagen on May 5, 1813, Kierkegaard became one of the most influential thinkers of the 19th century. His writings challenged people to examine their beliefs, decisions and relationships with the world rather than simply accepting the expectations of society.
Why Kierkegaard believed individual experience mattered

Kierkegaard is frequently described as a founding figure of existentialism, a philosophical tradition concerned with individual existence, freedom and the responsibility people have for their choices.

One of his central concerns was the difference between understanding something intellectually and actually living through it. He questioned the idea that human existence could be explained entirely through abstract theories or universal systems.

For Kierkegaard , becoming an individual involved making personal decisions and accepting the uncertainty that accompanied them. People could not simply rely on other people's expectations to determine how they should live.
This perspective helps explain why the popular quotation feels consistent with his broader philosophy, even if its attribution is questionable.

His personal life also influenced his writing. Kierkegaard spent much of his life in Copenhagen and became particularly interested in questions surrounding faith, anxiety, love and the individual's relationship with God.

His relationship with Regine Olsen was especially significant. The couple became engaged in 1840, but Kierkegaard subsequently broke off the engagement. The experience continued to influence his reflections on commitment, sacrifice and personal responsibility.

Among his most important publications were Either/Or (1843), Fear and Trembling (1843) and The Concept of Anxiety (1844). These works examined different aspects of human decision-making and the emotional consequences of living with uncertainty.
The real author behind the famous quotation

The history of the quotation adds another dimension to its meaning. Van der Leeuw 's The Conquest of Illusion, published in 1928, contains the earlier version of the sentence, predating many of the later appearances that credited Kierkegaard .

Reference collections including Wikiquote have highlighted the disputed attribution, while the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy provides a detailed account of Kierkegaard's actual philosophical contributions.
Ultimately, the quotation remains popular because its message is easy to recognise. Life cannot always be organised into neat objectives, and not every difficult experience has an immediate solution.
Its appeal lies in encouraging people to appreciate relationships, unexpected opportunities and ordinary moments instead of becoming consumed by what they have yet to achieve.
Kierkegaard died in Copenhagen on November 11, 1855, aged 42, but his influence on philosophy, theology and literature continues.

Whether readers encounter the famous sentence under his name or Van der Leeuw 's, its central idea remains relevant: existence is not simply something to manage or control. It is something to participate in, understand and experience.

articles.title: On Neptune, it rains diamonds, and some scientists have managed to make them on Earth using plastic bottles
articles.standfirst: The method could replace explosives in the industrial production of nanodiamonds
articles.summary: The method could replace explosives in the industrial production of nanodiamonds
articles.body:
Turning the plastic from a water bottle into diamonds sounds like science fiction, but it is already a reality in the laboratory. A team of physicists from the Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) and the University of Rostock , in Germany , has managed to produce ten trillion nanodiamonds with each laser shot at a thin sheet of PET, the material used for bottles.

The big breakthrough is not only creating them, but having managed to recover them intact for the first time. The results are published in the journal Diamond and Related Materials .

The process is simple in appearance. A high-power laser hits the plastic three times per minute and generates a shock wave that compresses it to about 100 gigapascals, nearly a million times atmospheric pressure. In just a few nanoseconds, the carbon rearranges itself and forms diamonds.

The challenge came afterward: the crystals are shot out at more than ten kilometers per second, like a meteorite, and any rigid surface would destroy them. The solution was to place a soft gel behind the plastic that slows the impact and, when dissolved in water, releases the particles intact.

Each diamond measures about three nanometers and contains around 3,000 carbon atoms. “It was a special moment after years of work” , summarizes Ben Heuser, the study’s first author.

From Neptune's diamond rain to quantum sensors

The research originated to simulate the interior of Uranus and Neptune , where it is believed that diamonds rain down from methane subjected to enormous pressures. Now, the method could offer an alternative to current industrial production, which uses explosives and produces crystals with metal residues that have to be cleaned with acid.

Nanodiamonds are already used for polishing and, since the new method makes it possible to dope them with other atoms, they could be adapted for quantum sensors or contrast agents in magnetic resonance imaging. That said, three shots per minute are still not enough for industry, and the team is already thinking about a laser capable of firing ten times per second.

articles.title: In Alaska, an entire town lives in the same 14-story building, which houses the post office and the police station: people go to school through a tunnel, and the road closes at night
articles.standfirst: One of the most spectacular places on the planet
articles.summary: One of the most spectacular places on the planet
articles.body:
There are remote cities and towns that most people know nothing about and would be unable to locate and, above all, they would be surprised if they knew the living conditions. In Alaska , for example, there is an entire town whose inhabitants live in the same 14-story building , which also houses the post office, the Town Hall, the grocery store, and the police station.

It is located on the shores of an Alaskan fjord, and the town is called Whittier , at the beginning of the Passage Canal . It is surrounded by the state's steep mountains and has just over 250 inhabitants .

One building houses 85% of the population

What is curious about this place lies precisely in the way those people live, and everything revolves around the Begich Towers, a 14-story building with 196 apartments . It is a kind of hotel at the foot of the glaciers where, according to local data, around 85% of the population lives . The other 15% is located in another building, although a smaller one.

Another striking fact is that Whittier has no streets with single-family homes or garden areas; instead, the entire town is the apartment block itself. It was built in the 1950s by the United States Army so that military personnel and their families could stay there, since it had been a strategic point during World War II .

Once the army left the area in the early 1960s, the city bought the building and in 1974 it was renamed Begich Towers, in honor of Nick Begich, an Alaska congressman who died in 1972 in a plane crash. Inside are all the amenities for the residents: city hall, the police station, the supermarket, the laundromat, the medical clinic, and the church occupy the lower floors.

articles.title: Epictetus, Philosopher: "Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants"
articles.standfirst: The ancient Stoic's famous message challenges the modern definition of success
articles.summary: The ancient Stoic's famous message challenges the modern definition of success
articles.body:
What does it really mean to be wealthy? For many people, the answer is connected to a large bank balance, an impressive home, expensive possessions or the freedom to purchase almost anything they desire.

However, an idea traditionally attributed to the Greek philosopher Epictetus offers a very different way of measuring prosperity.

"Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants" is a saying that encourages people to reconsider their relationship with money and material success.

Instead of making happiness dependent on acquiring more, it suggests that satisfaction can come from learning to appreciate what is already available.

The distinction is particularly relevant in a society where advertising, social media and consumer culture constantly introduce new things to desire.

A person might purchase a more expensive car, upgrade their phone or move into a larger home, only to discover that the excitement eventually disappears and another purchase becomes the next objective.

The philosophy behind the quotation questions that endless cycle. If someone continually increases their expectations, even considerable wealth might never feel sufficient.

By contrast, a person who understands what they genuinely need may experience a greater sense of freedom without possessing nearly as much.

There is an important historical qualification, however. Although the wording is widely attributed to Epictetus , researchers have not identified the exact sentence in his surviving works.

Nevertheless, the sentiment closely reflects the ideas found throughout his teachings on desire, self-control and the nature of happiness.

Why Epictetus believed happiness should not depend on possessions

Epictetus was one of the most influential representatives of Stoicism, a philosophical tradition that placed considerable importance on reason, personal responsibility and emotional discipline.

Born around 50–55 AD in Hierapolis, in what is now Turkey, he spent part of his early life enslaved in Rome. He eventually gained his freedom and became a teacher of philosophy, establishing a school in Nicopolis, in northwestern Greece.

His lessons were later preserved by his student Arrian in works including Discourses and The Enchiridion.

One of the central principles of his philosophy was the distinction between things within our control and things outside it.

In the opening chapter of The Enchiridion, Epictetus explains that our opinions, desires and decisions belong to us, while possessions, reputation, physical circumstances and other external factors do not offer the same certainty.

This idea provides an important foundation for understanding the quotation. Money and material goods can make life more comfortable, but they cannot guarantee lasting happiness. Their value can change, they can be lost, and they often create additional expectations.

Epictetus therefore encouraged people to focus on developing their character and controlling their reactions rather than allowing external circumstances to determine their emotional well-being.

The difference between wanting something and needing it

The quotation also raises an important question about the role of desire in everyday life.

Wanting a better lifestyle is not necessarily a problem. People can have ambitions, work towards financial security and enjoy the rewards of their efforts. The difficulty arises when every achievement creates another requirement for feeling satisfied.

For example, someone who earns more money might initially feel financially secure, but that feeling can disappear if their spending increases at the same pace. A bigger house leads to more expensive furniture, a new car creates additional costs, and luxury holidays become an expectation rather than an occasional pleasure.

The underlying problem is not necessarily the possessions themselves, but the belief that acquiring them will eventually provide permanent satisfaction.

Epictetus explored this relationship between desire and disappointment in The Enchiridion. His teaching suggests that people become vulnerable to frustration when they place their happiness in things that are not entirely within their control.

A lesson that remains relevant today

The message has particular significance in modern discussions about personal finance, where saving, budgeting and avoiding unnecessary debt are increasingly important.

Having fewer wants does not mean rejecting ambition, refusing to enjoy life or believing that money has no value. Financial resources can provide stability, protect families from unexpected expenses and create opportunities.

Instead, the philosophy encourages people to distinguish between spending that genuinely improves their lives and purchases driven by comparison, pressure or temporary excitement.

It also suggests that contentment is something people can develop rather than something they must purchase. Appreciating relationships, good health, meaningful experiences and personal achievements can provide satisfaction that expensive possessions cannot necessarily replace.

Ultimately, the saying traditionally associated with Epictetus challenges the assumption that wealth is measured by how much someone owns. Its deeper message is that a person who constantly needs more may never feel rich, regardless of their financial circumstances.

By learning to manage expectations and recognize what truly matters, people can develop a healthier relationship with money and material success.

In that sense, genuine prosperity may have less to do with the size of someone's possessions and more to do with their ability to live comfortably without endlessly searching for something else.

articles.title: NASA is looking for candidates to travel to and live on the Moon: these are the demanding requirements and the deadline
articles.standfirst: "They will demand technical excellence, good judgment, teamwork, and courage," says Jared Isaacman
articles.summary: "They will demand technical excellence, good judgment, teamwork, and courage," says Jared Isaacman
articles.body:
Do you want to go to the Moon? NASA is looking for new space explorers to travel to and live on Earth's satellite. The U.S. space agency is working to establish a small colony and, later, make the leap to Mars . It is a new era and the casting call is open. Although, to no one's surprise, the requirements and demands are very high . "The opportunity is here. The mission awaits us. And the only thing missing to complete the greatest adventure humanity has ever embarked on is you," says Matt Anderson , NASA's deputy administrator.

NASA's requirements for traveling to the moon

The process is open to anyone who meets these demanding requirements. First, it is necessary to have completed at least two years of a doctoral program in engineering, biological sciences, physical sciences, computer science, mathematics, medicine, physician assistant studies, nursing, or a similar specialty. Second, to have, or be currently enrolled in, a national-level test pilot program . Those who register for the selection must also have three years of experience in their professional field.

Ten selected from 8,000 applications in 2024

The selection process is extraordinarily thorough. The latest benchmark is the process that NASA opened in 2024 . At that time, a total of 8,000 candidates applied to become astronauts, and the United States space agency selected only ten people . After being selected, they will have to undergo two years of specific training. The deadline to submit the application is December 3 .

The golden age of space exploration

NASA has insisted that the agency is in a new golden era of space exploration. " The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Lunar Base , and contribute to the development of the systems and operations that will ultimately take crews to Mars. These missions will demand technical excellence, good judgment, teamwork, and courage ," says Jared Isaacman , NASA administrator.

articles.title: They offer 2,500 euros a month, with accommodation and food, to count penguins in Antarctica, but with no water for showering
articles.standfirst: You have to live for five months in Port Lockroy, on Goudier Island
articles.summary: You have to live for five months in Port Lockroy, on Goudier Island
articles.body:
People are not aware of the amount of work that exists in the rest of the world. Some, like the one we are going to explain below, could even seem surreal. The British organization UK Antarctic Heritage Trust (UKAHT) offers many citizens the chance to travel to Port Lockroy, on Goudier Island, to observe penguins.

There they will have to live for five months. They offer 2,500 euros per month , in addition to providing accommodation and food. The job consists of counting penguins, although other duties must also be carried out. For the 2026/2027 season, 14 people have already been selected and have placed themselves under the organization’s orders.

These are the duties of the workers at Port Lockroy, in Antarctica

Once the journey takes place, the workers are divided into two groups: eight stay in Port Lockroy. From there, tasks are distributed, such as monitoring the penguins, managing the museums, running the post office, and overseeing the local souvenir shop. The other six selected will have more research-oriented roles. The latter will be accompanied by healthcare and mountain professionals.

However, not everything is rosy. The salary and conditions are good, but there are also some drawbacks. “There is no running water or showers on the island, so the sanitary facilities are very basic. Water is collected in tanks from the ships that visit, which offer showers approximately once a week, but in adverse weather conditions, it can be up to two weeks without visits or showers,” the organization explains.

Camilla Nichol, director of UKAHT, explains that this year will also be special because they must face the challenges of “a rapidly warming climate.” In Antarctica, temperature rises of four degrees have been recorded.

articles.title: Cruise ship pianist rescued after falling overboard: survived nine hours adrift in the Pacific
articles.standfirst: After rescuing him: “I thought I was going to die”
articles.summary: After rescuing him: “I thought I was going to die”
articles.body:
the Royal Caribbean company has experienced one of those strange incidents that can happen on a cruise ... in this case it involves a pianist who worked on it and who ended up in the sea. He fell into the water and was rescued alive by some fishermen about 32 kilometers off the coast of California (USA) after spending almost nine hours adrift in the Pacific Ocean.

Last Friday, fishermen Grant Garret and Sean Norton spotted in the water, near Catalina Island, this man , about whom no further details have emerged so far, as reported by CBS and the British BBC, among other media outlets.

Reaction after finding him at sea

"The only thing he said to me was: "Thank you. I thought I was going to die"" , they said from Norton, adding that the man identified himself as a pianist on a 14-deck cruise ship . However, once on land, the cruise ship worker was taken conscious to a hospital and is in "stable" condition.

More specifically, it was a crew member from the cruise ship "Ovation of the Seas" who may have fallen in the early hours of the morning, about nine hours before being located . "He was approximately 15 to 20 miles off the coast, practically in the middle of the ocean," Adam Yacenda, head of Newport Beach lifeguards, told CBS.

This man's astonishing survival was attributed to the high temperatures currently being recorded in the Pacific , whose waters are around 24ºC due to the effects of the El Niño climate phenomenon. "In another year, there's no way he makes it" , they commented from Norton.

articles.title: Who is Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy setting Nvidia ablaze
articles.standfirst: Her name appears linked to private banking, journalism, and the company Megaspeed
articles.summary: Her name appears linked to private banking, journalism, and the company Megaspeed
articles.body:
Alice Huang is the name of the Chinese spy, according to United States intelligence services, who has sparked a fire at Nvidia , the tech giant. This woman, also known as Huan Le , maintained an extramarital relationship with Nvidia founder and CEO, Jensen Huang (his surname does not imply any family relation). The Chinese Government has denied that this woman is a spy .

Alice Huang was the director of Megaspeed International , dedicated to cloud services, a position she held until March 2023 . This Chinese company purchased Nvidia products worth 2 billion dollars . U.S. officials, according to The New York Times, visited its facilities in Singapore in 2024 and observed two strange details: there were only two employees and the Nvidia chips were still stored in their boxes . For this reason, there is speculation that Megaspeed may have been involved in smuggling chips into China.

Alice Huang: businesswoman, journalist, private banking...

Information about the past of Alice Huang was quick to emerge. Huan Le , according to EFE, appears in some media outlets as a businesswoman, but also as a journalist, with experience at Hunan TV and the state channel CCTV-1 . The alleged Chinese spy, as she is regarded by United States Intelligence, also appears linked to fund management in private banking. There is no information available about the current life of Alice Huang (or Huan Le) .

The photo of Alice Huang and Jensen Huang

The photograph circulating in the media and on social networks of Alice Huang and Jensen Huang corresponds to the Computex technology fair (in the Taiwanese city of Taipei, in 2024). Some platforms have manipulated the appearance of Alice Huang with Artificial Intelligence to make her look younger. "I assume full responsibility for what I did and for the harm I caused, and I accept the criticism that this entails," stated Nvidia's CEO in a statement.

U.S. officials, according to The New York Times, visited its facilities in Singapore in 2024 and observed two strange details: there were only two employees and the Nvidia chips were still stored in their boxes . Alice Huang: businesswoman, journalist, private banking...

Information about the past of Alice Huang was quick to emerge. Huan Le , according to EFE, appears in some media outlets as a businesswoman, but also as a journalist, with experience at Hunan TV and the state channel CCTV-1 . The alleged Chinese spy, as she is regarded by United States Intelligence, also appears linked to fund management in private banking. There is no information available about the current life of Alice Huang (or Huan Le) .

The photograph circulating in the media and on social networks of Alice Huang and Jensen Huang corresponds to the Computex technology fair (in the Taiwanese city of Taipei, in 2024). Some platforms have manipulated the appearance of Alice Huang with Artificial Intelligence to make her look younger. "I assume full responsibility for what I did and for the harm I caused, and I accept the criticism that this entails," stated Nvidia's CEO in a statement.

articles.title: Martin Luther, philosopher: "Beer is made by men, wine by God"
articles.standfirst: A figure who changed the way religion was understood in Europe
articles.summary: A figure who changed the way religion was understood in Europe
articles.body:
On November 10, 543 years ago, in 1483, Martin Luther was born , one of the most influential and well-known figures in Christianity . As the years go by, the sayings and accounts of this type of figure tend to endure over time and transcend through the years, just as happened with this German philosopher, considered the driving force behind the Protestant Reformation and Lutheranism.

Beyond the theories he promoted and more, he is remembered for a phrase attributed to him that brings together two of the most popular and widely consumed beverages in the world: “Beer is made by men, wine by God.”

This was Martin Luther, and this is the meaning of his quote about beer and wine

This expression, which commonly circulates associated with him, reflects a c omparison when it comes to producing both beverages. First of all, beer requires human intervention to transform its ingredients through a manufacturing process. On the other hand, wine is born from grapes, a fruit that comes from nature. For this reason, the phrase highlights the natural character of wine as opposed to the artisanal process of beer.

Martin Luther was born in Eisleben, in what is now modern-day Germany. He studied Law at the University of Erfurt, although he later entered a monastery of the Order of Saint Augustine and worked as a professor at the University of Wittenberg as a theologian. He changed forever the way religion was understood in Europe.

His confrontation with certain practices of the Catholic Church ended up triggering a reform movement that laid the foundations for Lutheranism , one of the main branches of Christianity.

On the other hand, he translated part of the Bible into German. Luther eventually died at the age of 62 on February 18, 1546, but his legacy continues to have great historical and religious significance.

articles.title: Epictetus, Philosopher: "Circumstances don't make the man, they only reveal him to himself”
articles.standfirst: An ancient stoic teaching offers a different way to understand failure, adversity and the unexpected challenges that shape our lives
articles.summary: An ancient stoic teaching offers a different way to understand failure, adversity and the unexpected challenges that shape our lives
articles.body:
People often believe they know themselves until something happens that disrupts their carefully established routines. A sudden job loss, the breakdown of a relationship or an unexpected personal disappointment can reveal reactions and emotions they never anticipated experiencing.

The ancient Greek philosopher Epictetus believed these moments offered an unusually revealing insight into human character. Rather than seeing difficult circumstances as experiences that automatically transform people, he argued that adversity exposes qualities already present beneath the surface.

"Circumstances don't make the man, they only reveal him to himself," is a saying widely attributed to Epictetus.

The observation challenges the familiar belief that hardship inevitably makes people stronger. While difficult experiences can encourage personal growth, they may also reveal insecurity, impatience or a reluctance to confront uncomfortable realities.

Someone who considers themselves confident might discover how heavily they depend on approval from others. Equally, a person who has always questioned their abilities may uncover unexpected courage when confronted with circumstances they cannot avoid.

According to stoic thinking, the defining factor isn't simply what happens to someone, but how they choose to respond.

Why difficult experiences expose our true character

Epictetus lived during the first and second centuries AD and became one of stoicism's most influential teachers, developing a philosophy centered on the distinction between events and our responses to them.

His teachings emphasized that individuals cannot control every circumstance they encounter, but they can examine their judgments, decisions and actions when those circumstances become difficult.

Two people might experience an identical professional setback yet interpret it in completely different ways. One may regard the disappointment as proof of personal failure, while another considers what can be learned before attempting something new.

Neither response changes what has already happened. However, the interpretation influences whether the experience becomes a source of lasting resentment or an opportunity for constructive reflection.

The philosopher's approach also challenges the assumption that comfort provides the clearest understanding of someone's personality. When life proceeds smoothly, qualities such as patience, courage and emotional discipline are rarely subjected to meaningful tests.

Adversity removes that protection, exposing how individuals behave when their expectations are challenged and familiar sources of reassurance disappear.

What Epictetus' philosophy teaches us

The relevance of this philosophy extends well beyond ancient Greece, particularly in a world where uncertainty can affect careers, relationships, finances and personal ambitions.

Modern discussions about resilience often suggest that every setback must produce a stronger, more successful individual. Epictetus ' ideas offer a more measured interpretation, emphasizing self-awareness rather than demanding an immediate positive outcome.

Not every difficult experience contains an obvious lesson, and surviving a painful period doesn't always leave someone feeling victorious. Sometimes, continuing through uncertainty represents the greatest achievement possible.

However, examining our reactions can reveal patterns that otherwise remain unnoticed, including fears that influence decisions or expectations that make disappointment harder to accept.

The central lesson is that personal growth begins with recognizing those responses rather than pretending they don't exist.

Ultimately, Epictetus ' observation suggests that life's most challenging moments can provide something ordinary circumstances rarely offer: an honest understanding of who we are when comfort, certainty and control are taken away.

articles.title: Umberto Eco, philosopher and writer: "The humorist is the one who calls into question the certainties of the powerful"
articles.standfirst: The italian reflects on the power of criticism to destabilize beliefs
articles.summary: The italian reflects on the power of criticism to destabilize beliefs
articles.body:
Often, human beings tend to believe as true everything that rulers, successful and influential businesspeople express out loud. Those ideas become absorbed into the collective and end up turning into certainties, even when they are not. That is where the power of criticism comes into play, the ability of, for example, comedians to destabilize that established power.

Umberto Eco , a renowned philosopher and writer of Italian origin, uttered one of the most famous and representative phrases of this school of thought. “The humorist is the one who casts doubt on the certainties of the powerful” , he said in one of his many reflections on the human being.

The role of humor in critical thinking

With these words, Eco refers to the ability of some people to, through humor, show some how what is regarded as absolute truth , perhaps because it has been proclaimed by official bodies, may not actually be so. For the thinker, noteworthy is the ability of humorists to offer other points of view .

His reflection, however, invites everyone to know how to discern in an aspect that he considers key in this matter. For him, it is important to differentiate between those sarcastic comments that are nevertheless legitimate and are intended only to provoke other points of view, and another kind of humor, the more destructive kind that merely seeks easy mockery and has no basis whatsoever.

On this, another of his best-known phrases about the role of humor stands out: "Laughter kills fear, and without fear there can be no faith , because without fear of the devil there is no longer any need for God." "The devil is not the prince of matter, the devil is the arrogance of the spirit, faith without a smile, truth that is never touched by doubt," he said in another of his reflections.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV surprises crowds with an unexpected gesture before going to bed
articles.standfirst: After a long day of public appearances in Argentina, the pontiff found a playful way to tell his supporters it was time to call it a night
articles.summary: After a long day of public appearances in Argentina, the pontiff found a playful way to tell his supporters it was time to call it a night
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV gave people gathered outside the Apostolic Nunciature in Buenos Aires an unexpected moment when he used a simple hand gesture to signal that he was ready to go to sleep . The move drew laughter from the crowd and even one of the security officers accompanying him.

The pontiff had initially greeted supporters from the building's balcony, but as people continued asking to see him, he decided to step outside and meet them on the sidewalk. Before saying goodnight, he brought his hands together beside his face, resting his head against them to imitate someone sleeping.

Pope Leo XIV shares a lighthearted moment with Argentine supporters

The gesture was a humorous way of letting the faithful know that his busy schedule had finally come to an end. After greeting those who had gathered to see him, Leo XIV repeated the same movement, making it clear that it was time for everyone to head home and get some rest.

His day had included several major engagements, beginning with a visit to the Don Orione Little Cottolengo in Claypole, followed by a large Mass in Buenos Aires. He also met with labor leaders, representatives of social movements and members of different religious communities before returning to the Nunciature.

A dinner with Argentine bishops included music and local dishes

Earlier that evening, the Pope had attended a private dinner with bishops at the Buenos Aires archdiocesan headquarters. According to El País , the meal featured traditional Argentine dishes, including empanadas, ribeye steak and flan with dulce de leche.

The dinner also included a musical tribute from the bishops, who sang songs for the pontiff , including Carlos Gardel's "Volver" and "Zamba de mi esperanza" by Los Chalchaleros. Leo XIV appeared visibly moved by parts of the gathering, which brought his second day in Argentina to a close before his scheduled trip to Córdoba.

articles.title: One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is being reconstructed after 2,200 years
articles.standfirst: Some of the discoveries have surprised even the specialists involved in the project
articles.summary: Some of the discoveries have surprised even the specialists involved in the project
articles.body:
T he Lighthouse of Alexandria stood as one of humanity’s greatest architectural achievements for centuries. Rising approximately 338 feet above Egypt’s Mediterranean coast , the monument guided ships into one of the ancient world’s most important harbors before earthquakes and centuries of deterioration brought it down.

Now, archaeologists have recovered enormous stone blocks weighing as much as 80 tons from the sea, providing an extraordinary opportunity to understand how the legendary structure was built. The discoveries have also helped researchers reconstruct the lighthouse in unprecedented detail, revealing an elaborate interior that remained largely unknown for centuries.

The recovery operation, combined with cutting-edge digital technology and historical research, has transformed what scientists know about one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. And some of the discoveries have surprised even the specialists involved in the project.

An ancient wonder hidden beneath the Mediterranean

Construction of the Lighthouse of Alexandria began in the early third century BC under Ptolemy I, the Macedonian general who took control of Egypt following the death of Alexander the Great. Designed by the Greek architect Sostratus of Cnidus , the lighthouse was built on the island of Pharos, near the entrance to Alexandria’s harbor. It served as a navigational landmark for approximately 1,600 years, making it one of the longest-lasting monumental structures of antiquity.

At roughly 103 meters tall, it dominated the surrounding coastline and became a symbol of Alexandria’s economic and cultural importance. However, earthquakes eventually sealed its fate. A particularly destructive earthquake in 1303 severely damaged the structure, which was subsequently abandoned. Over the following centuries, much of its surviving masonry was removed. In 1477, the Qaitbay Citadel was constructed on the same location, incorporating stones taken from the ancient lighthouse.

Much of what remained eventually collapsed into the Mediterranean. Underwater archaeological investigations began in 1995 under French archaeologist Jean-Yves Empereur. Since then, researchers have documented 4,896 stone blocks scattered across approximately two hectares of seabed, at depths between four and nine meters.

The site is considered the world’s largest submerged architectural complex. Yet those remains represent only about 10% of the original lighthouse. Reconstructing the monument from the surviving stones alone was therefore impossible.

That is where a remarkable recovery operation and an unusual collaboration between archaeologists and engineers came into play. Archaeologists bring 80-ton architectural pieces back to the surface

In June 2025, an international research team led by Isabelle Hairy, an architect-archaeologist at France’s National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS), recovered 22 massive stone blocks from the seabed.

Hairy has directed the underwater excavation since 1997

Using a crane mounted on a barge, the team brought some of the lighthouse’s most important architectural components above water. Among them were sections of the monumental entrance, including its lintel, doorjambs and threshold.

Some of the recovered blocks weighed between 70 and 80 tons. Other enormous slabs from the building’s foundation weighed approximately 40 tons each. These were not simply enormous pieces of ancient masonry. They represented architectural elements that could help researchers understand how the lighthouse was assembled and how its different sections fitted together.

One particularly significant discovery involved a pylon gateway, a monumental entrance structure traditionally associated with Egyptian architecture but incorporating Greek construction techniques. Its design reflected the cultural influences that shaped Alexandria during the Ptolemaic period, when Egyptian and Greek traditions existed side by side.

Each recovered stone was documented through photogrammetry, a technique that uses overlapping photographs to produce highly accurate three-dimensional models.

The resulting scans were combined with digital records of more than 100 architectural blocks previously documented underwater, creating an increasingly detailed database of the ancient monument. Recovering enormous stones was only part of the challenge. Researchers still needed to reconstruct the approximately 90% of the building that had disappeared.

articles.title: Nayib Bukele casts himself as Haiti’s ‘savior’ with a brutal offensive against gangs: ‘It will be free’
articles.standfirst: He has deployed 2,500 Salvadoran troops to Haiti
articles.summary: He has deployed 2,500 Salvadoran troops to Haiti
articles.body:
Salvadoran troops bombard a gangster’s home from helicopters over the Haitian countryside. Civilians cheer on marching camouflage-clad soldiers. Armored cars drive through the Caribbean nation’s gang-ravaged streets.

The videos flood the social media of Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, Salvadoran officials and an army of pro-government influencers with a simple message in a mix of Haitian Creole, English and Spanish: “We will help you take back your country ... Finally, Haiti will be free.”

It's part of Bukele's push to present himself as the savior to Haiti’s gang crisis.

By doing so, experts say the communications specialist-turned-president seeks to defuse mounting international scrutiny over his troops' deployment and drum up political support in his own country ahead of February elections.

But they say the offensive in Haiti is a high-stakes gamble that could both isolate allies like the Trump administration and dent popular support in his own country.

“It’s an electoral campaign to promote Nayib Bukele and portray him as if he’s a superhero. They're selling an Avengers movie,” said Salvadoran political communications strategist Roberto Dubon. “He's using Haiti as a testing ground to implement his policies on an international level.”

Bukele's political narrative

El Salvador ’s military offensive in Haiti began in mid-October, when four Salvadoran aviation technicians working with a U.N.-backed mission went missing in a gang attack. Since then, the government has sent 2,500 soldiers to the Caribbean country with little transparency or oversight.

The disappearances posed a challenge for Bukele, who gained international fame with a political narrative centered on beating back El Salvador’s gangs with a heavy hand.

As international scrutiny has mounted over the operation and a gang leader said that the four technicians are dead, the president’s narrative has shifted from rescuing the Salvadorans to eradicating Haiti’s gangs.

“We kept our promise,” Bukele posted on Tuesday, sharing a video of Salvadoran forces bombing a gang leader’s house after previously asking for the coordinates on X. “Most of them ran away without even trying to fight. What cowards!”

The tongue-in-cheek tone and images of soldiers mirror cinematic videos the government produces in its own country to craft a careful narrative around Bukele's gang crackdown, which has fueled accusations of mass human rights abuses.

In Haiti, just like in El Salvador, throngs of pro-government influencers quickly latched onto and magnified that message, said Dubon.

Juggling elections and international scrutiny

Meanwhile, Bukele gears up for February presidential elections, which he is all but guaranteed to win with fierce support for his crackdown on gangs. Polling puts approval for the president well over 90%.

Democratic concerns hang over the vote after the legislature controlled by Bukele’s party moved up elections from 2029 to 2027 and eliminated presidential term limits in the constitution — paving the way for the populist to stay in power indefinitely.

In the face of democratic criticisms, a lagging economy and Salvadorans normalizing newfound freedoms after years of not living in constant fear of the gangs, the Haiti offensive offers Bukele a tool to remind Salvadorans of his security wins ahead of the vote, said Luis Enrique Amaya, a Salvadoran security consultant.

“He has to construct this narrative of success (in Haiti) to strengthen his image as president,” Amaya said. “Bukele won’t allow even a centimeter of his popularity and legitimacy to be lost. Not even a millimeter, not a single vote.”

Bukele has toyed with the idea of taking his contentious anti-crime campaign abroad for years, but his current offensive is increasingly seen as a risky bet.

On Monday, the rights group Amnesty International called on El Salvador and Haiti's governments to publicly disclose the agreement allowing forces into Haiti, and to “comply with international human rights law." It warned of operations potentially exacerbating violence and affecting civilians.

The same day, Bukele ally U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio distanced himself from the Salvadoran offensive when speaking to press, saying the U.S. was “not actively involved.” He threw his support behind the U.N.-backed gang suppression force, of which El Salvador doesn't form part.

“There is no plan B,” Rubio said.

Securing ‘quick, symbolic victories’ in convoluted conflict

Security experts like Diego Da Rin, Haiti analyst for International Crisis Group, have cast doubt on Bukele's ability to replicate his model to vanquish Haiti's gangs.

Bukele debilitated El Salvador's two powerful gangs by suspending key constitutional rights and detaining more than 1% of the small Central American nation's population. The Salvadoran investigative news organization El Faro, whose staff has since been exiled from the country, also reported that Bukele had negotiated with those gangs.

Haiti's gang warfare is far more convoluted. Roughly two dozen well-known gangs operate in Port-au-Prince and dozens more have launched deadly attacks outside the capital. They have spent years leeching off political turmoil and overwhelmed police forces to make power grabs and sow terror.

They wield weapons smuggled mainly from the U.S. and are far more well-armed than Salvadoran gangs once were. They are deeply entwined with some of the country’s political elite, making it nearly impossible for Bukele to replicate his war on gangs.

That will either push Salvadoran troops into an extended conflict or, more likely, push Bukele to make quick shows of force to project victory before retiring troops, said Tiziano Breda, an analyst with Armed Conflict Location & Event Data.

Breda warned that costs incurred by the foreign offensive — Bukele's government has said it's footing the bill — could fester resentment in El Salvador, where one in four people still live in poverty.

Da Rin said that Salvadoran troops could pressure Haitian police and international forces to better organize and more effectively push back the gangs, something they have failed to do for years. But he warned it could also push rival gangs to unite and form coalitions, as has happened in the past.

Similar to El Salvador's own war on gangs, that could have a human toll, he warned, especially if Salvadoran troops don't operate under strict rules like the U.N.-backed force.

“The Salvadoran troops' eagerness to secure quick, symbolic victories entails huge risks for civilians who can be caught in the crossfire,” Da Rin said.

As international scrutiny has mounted over the operation and a gang leader said that the four technicians are dead, the president’s narrative has shifted from rescuing the Salvadorans to eradicating Haiti’s gangs.

“We kept our promise,” Bukele posted on Tuesday, sharing a video of Salvadoran forces bombing a gang leader’s house after previously asking for the coordinates on X. “Most of them ran away without even trying to fight. What cowards!”

The tongue-in-cheek tone and images of soldiers mirror cinematic videos the government produces in its own country to craft a careful narrative around Bukele's gang crackdown, which has fueled accusations of mass human rights abuses.
In Haiti, just like in El Salvador, throngs of pro-government influencers quickly latched onto and magnified that message, said Dubon.
Juggling elections and international scrutiny

Meanwhile, Bukele gears up for February presidential elections, which he is all but guaranteed to win with fierce support for his crackdown on gangs. Polling puts approval for the president well over 90%.

Democratic concerns hang over the vote after the legislature controlled by Bukele’s party moved up elections from 2029 to 2027 and eliminated presidential term limits in the constitution — paving the way for the populist to stay in power indefinitely.

In the face of democratic criticisms, a lagging economy and Salvadorans normalizing newfound freedoms after years of not living in constant fear of the gangs, the Haiti offensive offers Bukele a tool to remind Salvadorans of his security wins ahead of the vote, said Luis Enrique Amaya, a Salvadoran security consultant.

“He has to construct this narrative of success (in Haiti) to strengthen his image as president,” Amaya said. “Bukele won’t allow even a centimeter of his popularity and legitimacy to be lost. Not even a millimeter, not a single vote.”
Bukele has toyed with the idea of taking his contentious anti-crime campaign abroad for years, but his current offensive is increasingly seen as a risky bet.

On Monday, the rights group Amnesty International called on El Salvador and Haiti's governments to publicly disclose the agreement allowing forces into Haiti, and to “comply with international human rights law." It warned of operations potentially exacerbating violence and affecting civilians.

The same day, Bukele ally U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio distanced himself from the Salvadoran offensive when speaking to press, saying the U.S. was “not actively involved.” He threw his support behind the U.N.-backed gang suppression force, of which El Salvador doesn't form part.
“There is no plan B,” Rubio said.
Securing ‘quick, symbolic victories’ in convoluted conflict
Security experts like Diego Da Rin, Haiti analyst for International Crisis Group, have cast doubt on Bukele's ability to replicate his model to vanquish Haiti's gangs.

Bukele debilitated El Salvador's two powerful gangs by suspending key constitutional rights and detaining more than 1% of the small Central American nation's population. The Salvadoran investigative news organization El Faro, whose staff has since been exiled from the country, also reported that Bukele had negotiated with those gangs.

Haiti's gang warfare is far more convoluted. Roughly two dozen well-known gangs operate in Port-au-Prince and dozens more have launched deadly attacks outside the capital. They have spent years leeching off political turmoil and overwhelmed police forces to make power grabs and sow terror.

They wield weapons smuggled mainly from the U.S. and are far more well-armed than Salvadoran gangs once were. They are deeply entwined with some of the country’s political elite, making it nearly impossible for Bukele to replicate his war on gangs.

That will either push Salvadoran troops into an extended conflict or, more likely, push Bukele to make quick shows of force to project victory before retiring troops, said Tiziano Breda, an analyst with Armed Conflict Location & Event Data.

Breda warned that costs incurred by the foreign offensive — Bukele's government has said it's footing the bill — could fester resentment in El Salvador, where one in four people still live in poverty.

Da Rin said that Salvadoran troops could pressure Haitian police and international forces to better organize and more effectively push back the gangs, something they have failed to do for years. But he warned it could also push rival gangs to unite and form coalitions, as has happened in the past.
Similar to El Salvador's own war on gangs, that could have a human toll, he warned, especially if Salvadoran troops don't operate under strict rules like the U.N.-backed force.
“The Salvadoran troops' eagerness to secure quick, symbolic victories entails huge risks for civilians who can be caught in the crossfire,” Da Rin said.

articles.title: Scientists discover troubling activity beneath the ocean near Japan’s massive earthquake fault
articles.standfirst: The underwater fault responsible for Japan’s devastating 2011 earthquake is showing signs of renewed stress, raising concerns about future seismic activity across the Pacific
articles.summary: The underwater fault responsible for Japan’s devastating 2011 earthquake is showing signs of renewed stress, raising concerns about future seismic activity across the Pacific
articles.body:
S cientists have found that the massive fault beneath the Japan Trench has returned to a locked state , meaning the tectonic plates are once again becoming stuck as they continue moving against each other. This process allows pressure to accumulate beneath the ocean floor, potentially setting the stage for another powerful earthquake .

The findings are particularly concerning because the same fault generated the magnitude 9.0 earthquake in March 2011 , which triggered a devastating tsunami along Japan’s northeastern coast. The disaster killed or left missing approximately 20,000 people and caused widespread destruction , including the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear crisis.

The fault has started building pressure again

The research, led by Fumiaki Tomita of Tohoku University, was published in the journal Science on November 5, 2026. Scientists analyzed 14 years of measurements taken from the ocean floor , combining them with observations from land, recurring earthquake data and computer models to understand how the fault changed after the 2011 disaster .

Their analysis revealed that the slow movement along the fault following the earthquake had almost completely stopped after approximately a decade. As a result, the boundary between the Pacific and continental plates has recovered a level of locking similar to the one recorded before the 2011 earthquake . This means the area has resumed accumulating energy that could eventually be released through another major seismic event.

Why scientists are concerned about another major earthquake

The discovery has implications beyond Japan. A powerful earthquake beneath the Pacific can generate tsunami waves that travel across the ocean, potentially affecting distant coastlines, including Hawaii and parts of the United States . The 2011 disaster demonstrated how far-reaching these events can be, with waves crossing the Pacific and causing damage along the US West Coast.

The renewed activity beneath the Japan Trench has raised questions about the potential threat to the US coastline. However, the latest research does not establish that another earthquake is imminent or provide a date for a future rupture. Instead, it shows how quickly a fault responsible for one of the most destructive earthquakes in recent history can return to storing seismic energy. The findings also highlight why scientists cannot rely exclusively on historical intervals between major earthquakes when assessing future risks. Although giant earthquakes along the Japan Trench have historically been associated with long recurrence periods, the recovery of the fault's locked state shows that the process of accumulating energy can happen much sooner than expected. Researchers believe continued monitoring of the ocean floor will be essential to understanding how these underwater faults behave and how their conditions evolve over time. The new evidence provides another reason to improve earthquake and tsunami preparedness, particularly for communities located along the Pacific coastline.
