articles.title: El Niño triggers unprecedented WHO response as global health fears grow
articles.standfirst: The World Health Organization has activated its highest operational response level for the 2026–27 event
articles.summary: The World Health Organization has activated its highest operational response level for the 2026–27 event
articles.body:
A s COP31 opened in Antalya, Türkiye , the World Meteorological Organization said the anticipated health impacts of El Niño had been classified as a health emergency for the first time. The WMO’s climate update warns that the event could intensify extreme weather and add pressure to communities already facing serious health risks.

The WHO’s response is a Grade 3 activation, which calls for a “major to maximal” operational effort. Its plan, published Nov. 2, covers October 2026 through September 2027 and sets out work on disease monitoring, prevention, health care and coordination with governments. The agency estimates it will need about $35 million for the first six months.

El Niño adds pressure to a warming world

WMO says the event is expected to strengthen toward the end of 2026 and continue into early 2027. January through September was already among the warmest periods on record, with the global average temperature about 1.47°C above the 1850–1900 average.

The agency says human-caused warming is loading the climate system with heat, while El Niño releases additional heat from the ocean and shifts weather patterns.

The health risks can build on one another. Extreme heat and drought can raise illness and death rates, worsen food and water shortages and increase wildfire smoke and poor air quality.

Heavy rainfall and flooding can bring injuries, disrupt medical services and increase exposure to diseases such as cholera, malaria and dengue.

The risks are expected to vary by region. PAHO has warned that drought, water scarcity, food insecurity and wildfires may affect parts of Central America, the Caribbean, northern South America and the Amazon Basin.

Wetter conditions could increase flood, landslide and disease risks in parts of the Andes, southern South America and the southern United States.

In Africa, authors of a recent Lancet commentary warn that the event could intensify existing health and humanitarian pressures, including heat, drought, flooding and disease outbreaks.

They urge the WHO to consider declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. That is a separate designation from the WHO’s Grade 3 operational response.

The warning comes after a deadly European summer: researchers estimated more than 50,000 heat-related excess deaths across 854 cities in June, July and August 2026, with about two-thirds linked to human-caused climate change.

As COP31 negotiations continue, the WHO’s response plan puts public-health preparedness alongside the wider challenge of limiting the warming that magnifies the harm of climate extremes.

articles.title: Scientists Discover Thriving Hidden Ecosystem Inside Metallic Nodules on the Pacific Ocean Floor
articles.standfirst: Thousands of tiny species have been found
articles.summary: Thousands of tiny species have been found
articles.body:
An international team of scientists has recently discovered that the polymetallic nodules on the Pacific Ocean floor harbor a hidden ecosystem with thousands of tiny species inside them. This unique habitat is at risk of disappearing due to deep-sea mining before science can fully study it.

The study was carried out in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone (CCZ), a vast abyssal region between Mexico and Hawaii. The researchers analyzed 244 nodules and found a total of 4,139 organisms living in their cracks and internal pores . These metal-rich stones function as three-dimensional habitats where animals less than one millimeter in size reside. The communities are dominated by nematodes, copepods, and foraminifera.

The nodules contain strategic metals such as nickel, copper, and cobalt

Genetic analyses by professionals confirmed that the organisms living inside the nodules are different from those living in the surrounding marine sediment. In addition, the largest specimens have wider cracks and concentrate a greater amount of life. The research was published in the journal Scientific Reports and was led by the Marum center at the University of Bremen together with institutes from the Netherlands, Belgium, and France.

It should be noted that the nodules contain strategic metals such as nickel, copper, and cobalt , which are in high demand for manufacturing batteries and electric vehicles. Therefore, the Clarion-Clipperton Zone is one of the main targets of future deep-sea mining.

These mineral formations grow at a rate of just a few millimeters per million years. As co-author Sabine Gollner warned in remarks reported by 20 minutos, their commercial extraction would cause an irreversible loss of unique species that have not even been described yet . “This must be taken into account in the environmental management of deep-sea mining,” the expert concludes.

articles.title: Friedrich Nietzsche, philosopher: "Man is a bridge stretched between the animal and the Superman"
articles.standfirst: Nihilism and the contemporary crisis of values can be confronted by embracing the moral void implied by the death of God, reflecting on Nietzsche and the search for new vital meanings.
articles.summary: Nihilism and the contemporary crisis of values can be confronted by embracing the moral void implied by the death of God, reflecting on Nietzsche and the search for new vital meanings.
articles.body:
The constant search for direction in life is a universal human challenge that often becomes intertwined with frustration and the fear of making mistakes . In a world where happiness is presented as an elusive goal, many feel trapped in a cycle of external expectations and anxiety about the future. Reflecting on this reality, Nietzsche states that man can be seen as a bridge between the animal and the Superman , suggesting that our personal evolution is at stake.

This journey toward self-discovery, however, can generate loneliness and difficult relationships, further complicating the search for meaning . The ability to enjoy life is diminished when, caught between our limitations and aspirations, we confront the abyss of our own existential contradictions .

Man is a bridge stretched between the animal and the Superman

The bridge to the Overman: Nietzsche's concept

Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche (1844-1900) was a German philosopher who revolutionized contemporary thought and challenged the moral and religious norms of his time . His work has profoundly influenced modern philosophy, literature, and art, standing out for its critique of traditional morality and its concept of the will to power. Nietzsche is known for iconic phrases, such as "Man is a bridge between the animal and the Superman," which encapsulate his view of the human being as a creature in constant evolution and self-overcoming.

Nietzsche's thought is framed within a critique of nihilism and the death of God , an idea that holds that the loss of absolute values in modern society causes a crisis of meaning. His work "Thus Spoke Zarathustra" introduces concepts such as the Übermensch, which symbolizes an ideal of overcoming and creating new values, challenging established morality. Nietzsche is also connected with other thinkers, such as Arthur Schopenhauer, although distancing himself from his pessimism, as well as Heidegger and Foucault, who find in his critique of modernity a source of inspiration for their own philosophies.

articles.title: A mini-moon has been orbiting the Earth for several months: astronomers confirm its existence
articles.standfirst: Experts believe that this has been happening since last April
articles.summary: Experts believe that this has been happening since last April
articles.body:
Observing space is one of the greatest contributions to the advancement of humankind in its goal of continuing to expand its knowledge about everything that surrounds planet Earth . At that point, the work carried out by Krisztián Sárneczky , an astronomer who, in August 2026, discovered a small object orbiting around our planet, becomes important.

Research published by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center has confirmed that that object, named 2026 QQ8 , is actually a small celestial body, classified as a mini-moon barely one meter across .

How long will the Earth have a mini-moon in its orbit

Curiously, in reality it is a second moon that will accompany the Earth temporarily, since its gravity has become bound to ours , in the so-called Hill sphere, so it does not orbit under the influence of the Sun, but rather of the Earth. According to the data, this has been happening since last April and everything indicates that it will come to an end next December , when it will move into an orbit around the Sun.

Apparently, approximately every 10 years a situation similar to that of 2026 QQ8 can occur, in addition to the fact that it orbits at 1.48 times the distance from the Earth to the Moon and, if it were to reach the Earth's atmosphere, it would not take long to disintegrate due to its tiny size. Other mini-moons, in fact, have already gone through something similar at other times: 2020 SO, 2020 CD3 or 2024 PT5 .

Experts agree that other very small asteroids can spend a short period of time orbiting in areas linked to the Earth until they eventually separate and go on to do so in a zone under the Sun’s influence.

articles.title: First camping trip turns into six-day ordeal as missing teen is found alive in Australian bush
articles.standfirst: His friend raised the alarm when he failed to return, setting off a search
articles.summary: His friend raised the alarm when he failed to return, setting off a search
articles.body:
A weekend camping trip became a six-day search after 17-year-old William disappeared in dense bushland in Victoria’s east. He had gone with another teenager to camp near Walhalla, about 180 kilometers (112 miles) from Melbourne, but was unfamiliar with the area and had little experience outdoors, his mother, Elizabeth Barkley, told ABC News. A family friend later described it as William’s first camping trip.

William was last seen around 4 p.m. on Nov. 6 near Stoney Creek Road, between Cowwarr and Walhalla. His mother had dropped the teenagers off for the weekend. William walked back toward the drop-off point to collect more camping equipment, including an esky a cooler used to carry food and drinks but did not return. His phone, food and water were left behind.

A police helicopter spotted William’s tackle box

His friend searched and called out for him before reporting him missing, according to police and ABC News. A couple in a white utility vehicle also stopped to help the friend and drove him back toward the meeting point. Police launched a search shortly after the report, bringing in specialist officers, dogs, drones, divers, volunteers and the Police Air Wing.

William’s mother said he became disoriented and slipped down a steep drop, leaving him unable to get back up. Reports after his rescue said he had water from the creek and a packet of chips. For days, searchers worked through thick terrain and cold nights, while his family waited for news. His mother had told ABC that he was unfamiliar with the area and had a poor sense of direction.

The breakthrough came Thursday morning, when the police helicopter spotted a tackle box in bushland about two kilometers east of Stoney Creek. The crew zoomed in and saw William lying beside a creek. Flight officers winched him to safety and took him to the search command post, where he was reunited with his mother. Police said he was in good spirits and generally good health; he was taken to hospital for monitoring.

The relief followed days of fear for Barkley, who had described the disappearance as one of her worst nightmares. After William was found, she said she was overjoyed he was alive and joked that he was “grounded for life.”

Victoria Police advises people heading into the bush to tell a reliable person their route and expected return time, carry extra food, water and clothing, and bring a map and compass rather than relying only on a phone or GPS. If lost, police say to stay calm, find shelter, stay in one place and make yourself visible to searchers.
